children.name: Cormobates
children.description: A genus containing the single species of Australasian treecreeper found outside Australia, ranging into New Guinea. Unlike other treecreepers, it has a straight rather than decurved bill. It climbs tree trunks in a spiral pattern, probing bark crevices for insects.

children.name: Cormobates leucophaea
children.description: The white-throated treecreeper (Cormobates leucophaea) is an Australian treecreeper found in the forests of eastern Australia. It is also called Dilmun in the Gathang language of the Worimi people, who reside in eastern Port Stephens and Great Lakes regions of coastal New South Wales, Australia. The Dilmun is the totem of Worimi women. It is unrelated to the northern hemisphere treecreepers. It is a small passerine bird with predominantly brown and white plumage and measuring some 15 cm (6 in) long on average. It is insectivorous, eating mainly ants. Unlike treecreepers of the genus Climacteris, the white-throated treecreeper does not engage in cooperative breeding, and wherever it overlaps with species of that genus, it feeds upon much looser bark besides typically using different trees.

children.name: Climacteris
children.description: The typical Australasian treecreepers with subtly curved bills, found across Australia in a variety of wooded habitats. They are characterised by bold eyebrow stripes and chestnut rumps that are conspicuous in flight. Socially they exhibit cooperative breeding in several species, with young from previous broods assisting at the nest.

children.name: Climacteris erythrops
children.description: The red-browed treecreeper (Climacteris erythrops) is a species of bird in the family Climacteridae. It is endemic to temperate and subtropical eastern Australia. It is found in mature eucalypt forests and woodlands in both coastal and mountainous regions, from central Victoria to south-eastern Queensland.

children.name: Climacteris picumnus
children.description: The brown treecreeper (Climacteris picumnus) is the largest Australasian treecreeper.

children.name: Climacteris rufus
children.description: The rufous treecreeper (Climacteris rufus) is a species of bird in the family Climacteridae.

children.name: Climacteris melanurus
children.description:
The black-tailed treecreeper (Climacteris melanurus) is a species of bird in the family Climacteridae. It is endemic to north and northwestern Australia and is the only treecreeper species found throughout most of its range. It belongs to the genus Climacteris and is noticeably darker than the other members of the genus.
Its natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Climacteris affinis
children.description: The white-browed treecreeper (Climacteris affinis) is the smallest of the Australo-papuan treecreepers and sole family member adapted to arid environments. The species foraging strategy involves climbing the trunks of trees in search of invertebrate prey on and under bark. Although some populations within the species range have declined, the species IUCN conservation status is of Least Concern.

children.name: Climacteris placens
children.description: A small treecreeper found in the montane forests of New Guinea at elevations between 600 and 3,000 metres. It has brown upperparts, a pale eyebrow, and finely streaked pale underparts. It is the only Climacteris species found outside Australia and inhabits mossy montane forests, where it probes bark for insects in the typical treecreeper fashion.
